opening_message:
Ticket 1: Keith Mclaughlin (employee ID E032) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E032.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Employee E032 (Keith Mclaughlin) is a full-time Analyst. Requested write access to Source Code. Full-time employees may have up to write; Analyst does not own Source Code, so admin is not applicable. Write is within policy — recommend granting write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows E032 (Keith Mclaughlin) is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time as previously noted. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Basic training caps access at read; requested write exceeds this, so recommend granting read.
reason: E032 (Keith Mclaughlin) requested write access to Source Code. The Security note corrects the earlier HR note: the employee is a contractor with basic security training, not full-time. Per policy, contractors may have read, or write only with advanced security training. With basic training, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so grant the maximum allowed level: read.

content.text:
Let me analyze this ticket.

Employee Keith Mclaughlin (E032) requests write access to Source Code.

There are two notes with conflicting information:
- Note 1 says full_time Analyst, recommends write.
- Note 2 says contractor with basic security training, recommends read.

The security note (Note 2) appears to be the correction - it explicitly says "not full-time as previously noted." The HR note might be earlier/wrong, and the security DB note corrects it.

According to policy:
- contractor employees: read, or write if they have advanced security training. Never admin.
- This contractor has basic security training, so max is read.
- Requested write is above max, so grant read.

So I should grant read.

Let me submit decision: read.
